old: Principal findings: the selection scan. The BayPass scan returns 19 SNPs above a calibrated XtX threshold of 10.84, of which 13 also pass a 10% false-discovery threshold; 3.9 false positives are expected at the quantile threshold and the empirical FDR there is 20.6%. Seventeen of the 19 fall in 13 annotated genes; two are intergenic, including one (Pf3D7_11_v3:1,054,447, XtX 20.79, q = 0.005) that ranks fifth in the whole scan and survives FDR correction, the other being Pf3D7_12_v3:715,788 (XtX 15.09, q = 0.017). The 13 genes are headed by PTP7 (max XtX 26.44), the amino-acid transporter AAT1 (PF3D7_0629500, max XtX 24.20), FIKK4.2, ACS8 and NT2. A call-quality audit of all 19 outliers against the other 3,897 scanned SNPs clears the set as a whole: every significant difference runs in the outliers' favour (higher VQSLOD, p = 0.008; QD, p = 0.016; QUAL, p = 0.007), none has MQ < 50, strand bias or read-position bias, all 19 are RegionType Core, and the eight SNPs in exported-protein genes - the subset most open to a repetitive-family artefact worry - are in fact the cleanest in the panel (FS = 0.00 for all eight, MQ median 60.00, VQSLOD significantly higher than the rest), so that concern is not supported. The audit does, however, downgrade two adjacent chromosome-11 sites to lower confidence: Pf3D7_11_v3:1,054,447 itself and Pf3D7_11_v3:1,054,078 (SNRPF, XtX 13.98, q = 0.031), 369 bp apart, the two lowest-InbreedingCoeff sites in the panel (0.193 and 0.147), with 1,054,078 carrying ExcessHet = 69.59, the only nonzero value among all 3,916 SNPs and roughly 400x the genome-wide maximum. In a near-haploid organism that points to collapsed paralogy or copy-number variation rather than to mismapping, whose MQ and FS signatures are both clean here; the mechanism is unverified and a read-level depth check would settle it. The consequence is that the fifth-ranked outlier in the whole scan is one of the two least secure entries in it. The AAT1 outlier is pfaat1 Ser258Leu, the second-highest XtX in the scan and the only outlier variant with a published gene-editing phenotype - though pfaat1 appears nowhere in the WHO marker compendium at any tier and is not a WHO-classified marker. Several other outlier genes are functionally characterised in the literature at gene level (PTP7, an EMP1 trafficking protein; NT2; ACS8), so the claim is variant-level and not a claim of unique annotation. Amambua-Ngwa et al. (2023, Nature Microbiology) edited S258L into parasites and measured a 1.5-fold rise in chloroquine IC50, in a single chloroquine-resistant Southeast Asian line (NHP4026), with epistasis between S258L and F313S and an explicit pfcrt-background caveat; it is therefore a variant that potentiates chloroquine resistance modestly and conditionally, not a stand-alone resistance determinant, and the longitudinal 0% to 97% rise that paper reports is Gambian (1984-2014) and says nothing about Ghana. S258L survives FDR correction (q = 0.005) and falls from 0.824 in coastal savanna to 0.544 in Guinea savanna (four-zone chi-square p = 1.9 x 10 to the -18), with deciduous forest at 0.735 and the transitional zone at 0.640 - so for this one variable the four zones do fall in strict south-to-north order, the sole variable reported here in which the transitional zone does not break the ordering. The second AAT1 outlier is a synonymous site 883 bp away, so this is one signal with a linked silent site, not two independent lines of evidence.

old: [Observed] Two incidents during the final runs, recorded because the verification argument depends on them. First, results/baypass/xtx_all_snps.csv was found at 0 bytes, truncated at 08:29:53 - hours after the 01:42 run that produced it, so almost certainly a stray shell redirect where a read was intended during a verification pass. It was the only zero-byte file under results/ or interim/. It was regenerated from the intact BayPass outputs, and the regeneration is provably faithful rather than merely plausible: outlier_snps.bed, xtx_calibration.json and xtx_threshold.txt are byte-identical by md5 before and after, and the restored file carries the same 3,916 rows and the same 19 outliers. Second, the --suffix patch to step03_umap.py suffixed the file writes but not the print statements, so the run reported writing to the published dimred_comparison.csv when it had in fact correctly written dimred_comparison_qcset.csv. No data were at risk - the published file's mtime and contents were both checked - but a log that misreports its own output path is exactly what produces a later misattribution, and it was caught by inspecting the output directory rather than by reading the log. Both are fixed.

old: Sequencing study (new in this version). Pf8 isolates arrive through named partner studies, and in Ghana those studies are almost perfectly nested within zones. Four of the six zone pairs share no study whatsoever - coastal savanna versus Guinea savanna, coastal savanna versus transitional, deciduous forest versus Guinea savanna, and deciduous forest versus transitional - and the first of these is the pair behind the maximum FST and the polyclonality contrast. Each zone is dominated by one study: the transitional zone is 100% one study (1083-PF-GH-CONWAY, 50 of 50), coastal savanna 89% (387 of 435, 1241-PF-GH-ANINAGYEI), Guinea savanna 74% (2,678 of 3,605, 1168-PF-GH-AMENGA-ETEGO-SM) and deciduous forest 48% (391 of 815, 1200-PF-GH-MAIGA-SM). Batch effects in this dataset are demonstrable, not hypothetical: holding zone constant so that only study varies, call rate differs between the six studies within Guinea savanna at p = 2.8 x 10 to the -197. Deciduous forest draws on five studies in all; across the four of them large enough to test (811 of the zone's 815 isolates, the fifth contributing only 4) call rate differs at p = 7.7 x 10 to the -88, and the polyclonal fraction ranges from 0.430 to 0.578 (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0019).

old: [Observed] Batch effects in these data are demonstrable rather than hypothetical. Holding zone constant, so that only study varies, per-isolate call rate differs sharply between studies within the same zone (Table 2.6): within the Guinea savanna, across its six studies, Kruskal–Wallis H = 923.0, p = 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁹⁷, n = 3,605; within the deciduous forest, across the four of its five studies large enough to test, H = 406.7, p = 7.7 × 10⁻⁸⁸, n = 811. Within the deciduous forest those same four studies also differ in Fws (Kruskal–Wallis H = 14.9, p = 1.9 × 10⁻³, n = 811), and their polyclonal fractions span 0.430 to 0.578 — a spread comparable in size to the between-zone polyclonality differences reported in §6.2. The Guinea savanna shows no significant within-zone difference in Fws (H = 9.17, p = 0.103), so its p = 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁹⁷ is a statement about call rate alone and not about polyclonality. The coastal savanna, with two studies, shows no significant within-zone difference on either statistic; the transitional zone cannot be tested at all, because it is one study.

Table 2.6. Within-zone differences between sequencing studies, QC-passing isolates. Kruskal–Wallis tests on per-isolate call rate and on F_ws, computed within each zone so that zone is held constant and only study varies. From results/batch_within_zone_tests.csv. The deciduous forest test excludes a four-isolate study (1114-PF-PDN-DBS-GH-GHANSAH), hence 4 of 5 studies and n = 811 against 815 in Table 2.4. The two p-value columns are tests on the call-rate and F_ws distributions; no test of the polyclonal fraction itself exists in the outputs, so the last column is a range only and carries no p-value.

old: [Interpreted] The practical reading is as follows. Study confounding does not threaten the central finding that differentiation is very low, because what that finding supplies is a ceiling on magnitude rather than a positive claim: batch effects, if anything, inflate apparent between-group differences, so a batch-confounded design that still returns FST ≈ 0.002 is reporting an upper bound on true differentiation rather than a false positive. It does threaten any positive between-zone claim — the maximum-FST pair, the polyclonality gradient, the ADMIXTURE minor-component ordering, and the marker-frequency differences in §6.9 — because for the pairs concerned there is no study-level control to appeal to. Each of those claims should be read as "differs between zones, which in these data means between zone, region, period and sequencing batch jointly".
new: [Interpreted] The practical reading is as follows. Study confounding does not threaten the central finding that the observed differentiation is very low, but neither does that finding bound the true differentiation: batch effects can move an observed between-group contrast in either direction — through cohort composition, calling differences and differential missingness — so a batch-confounded design that still returns FST ≈ 0.002 is reporting a low observed value whose relation to the true value is not established, not an upper bound on it. It does threaten any positive between-zone claim — the maximum-FST pair, the polyclonality gradient, the ADMIXTURE minor-component ordering, and the marker-frequency differences in §6.9 — because for the pairs concerned there is no study-level control to appeal to. Each of those claims should be read as "differs between zones, which in these data means between zone, region, period and sequencing batch jointly".

old: TreeMix (Stage 7). A maximum-likelihood population graph is fitted with 0 to 5 migration edges, rooted on Guinea savanna, using a jackknife block size of 50 SNPs, which on the final 3,916-SNP panel gives roughly 78 blocks. Model fit is summarised as the proportion of variance in between-population covariance explained, computed over off-diagonal entries only, matching TreeMix's own definition. The sweep is now run with -se, which was omitted previously; without it every migration line in the .treeout file reads "weight NA NA NA" and no edge can be tested, so model choice had to rest on variance explained alone — a rule of thumb with no null distribution behind it. That is the objection, and it is not that variance explained is monotone in m: on this project's own output it is not. results/treemix/variance_explained.csv gives 0.896997, 0.940513, 0.996907, 0.999664, 0.999579, 0.999586 for m = 0 to 5, so it falls between m = 3 and m = 4. Nor is it true that variance explained cannot identify a stopping point: results/treemix/model_selection.json records a rule that does — the smallest m reaching 0.998 (step07c_plot_treemix.py:45), which gives m = 3 over 0 to 5, with a plateau fallback within 0.001 of the best (:46) giving m = 2 over 0 to 2, and that pair is where the superseded manuscript's "m = 3 (full), m = 2 (identifiable)" came from. The rule picks a number; what it cannot do is attach an error rate to it. With -se, TreeMix computes a jackknife mean and standard error for each migration weight and a p-value against zero, so the number of supported edges becomes a testable question rather than a judgement call. This is also what Section 5.5's change to the block size was for: the stated rationale, that too few blocks make the migration-edge tests unreliable, presupposes that such tests exist, and until -se was passed they did not.

old: [Observed] The single Asn458Asp call was confirmed at read level and is genuine. Because one call in 1,866 at a validated marker codon could as easily be an annotation or base-calling artefact as a real variant, the underlying data were retrieved. Codon 458 draws on Pf3D7_13_v3 positions 1,725,626, 1,725,625 and 1,725,624. The middle position carries no variant record. The last fails the release filter and has no non-reference carrier among the 1,900. The first, 1,725,626, passes the filter and is triallelic (REF T, ALT A and C, numalt = 2), which is why the numalt == 1 ingest mask excluded it from the genome-wide matrix. Isolate PF0106-C is homozygous for the second ALT, C, with allele depths of 0, 0 and 40 — forty of forty reads supporting that allele — at DP 40 and GQ 99, the maximum. On the minus strand C complements to G, turning the reference codon AAT into GAT, which is Asp. The call is unambiguous at the read level and the reconstruction is arithmetically correct. It is also not the validated allele: WHO validates N458Y, which requires AAT to TAT, a different substitution at the same base. So codon 458 is 0.9995 reference rather than fixed, the one alternative residue is Asp and not Tyr, and no WHO-screened artemisinin marker is observed.

old: [Observed] Those conditions occur in this panel, and they change nothing in it. Of the 125 variant records sitting exactly at the 171 panel positions, 16 carry at least one length-changing ALT and 2 have a multi-base REF; a further 19 records anchored outside the panel have a REF span covering a panel position. Genotypes were retrieved for all 32 affected records across all 1,900 isolates. Three have any homozygous non-reference carrier: pfcrt codon 76 with 133, pfcrt codon 271 with 138, and pfdhps codon 431 with 26. In every case the carriers sit on a supported, equal-length allele — codon 76 on ALT1 C, with none on the 55-base insertion; codon 271 on ALT1 GAACGTAAGA, with none on ALT2, none on the spanning deletion and none on the single-base C; codon 431 on ALT1 G, with none on the spanning deletion and none on the 20-base insertion. No isolate anywhere in the panel carries a length-changing allele as a homozygous call, and the 62 mixed calls at these records are removed by the mixed-call rule regardless. The counts reconcile exactly with the reported table: Lys76Thr 133, Gln271Glu 138, Ile431Val 26, and homozygous-reference counts of 1,741 and 1,735 against reported reference-residue counts of 1,741 and 1,735. No residue anywhere in the panel is X, which confirms independently that no spanning-deletion allele was ever substituted. The two multi-base REF records differ from the reference at their first base only, so applying one base loses nothing here. And none of the 57 codons is record-free, so the convention of reading absence as reference never determines a reported residue. The limitation is real and bounds what the implementation may be applied to; on these inputs it moves no published number. What still rests on an assumption is callability: a codon is called when its constituent genotypes are present and unmixed, which is a statement about the genotype array and not an independent measurement of per-isolate coverage.

old: [Calculated] Two printed edge p-values are floating-point artefacts, three more are visibly imprecise, and a single mechanism accounts for all five. An earlier version of this paragraph said that five of six values reproduced to three significant figures; that was wrong, and the corrected accounting follows. Recomputing every migration-edge p-value in m = 0 to 5 as a one-sided normal tail from the printed jackknife mean and standard error gives fifteen edges, of which thirteen carry a finite printed value and two print “< 2.22507 × 10⁻³⁰⁸”. That figure is exactly DBL_MIN, the smallest normal double-precision float, and it appears at m = 3 edge 2 (z = 10.53, stable tail 3.18 × 10⁻²⁶) and again at m = 4 edge 2 (z = 9.33, stable tail 5.45 × 10⁻²¹). Of the thirteen finite values, ten reproduce to three significant figures. The three that do not are m = 1 edge 1 (0.8% relative error), m = 2 edge 2 (14.2%) and m = 5 edge 2 (3.1%), and all three sit at z ≥ 7.8. The mechanism is computation of the upper tail as 1 − Φ(z) in double precision: near z = 8 the cumulative probability lies within about one unit in the last place of 1, so the subtraction destroys most of the significand. Evaluating 1 − fl(Φ(8.060)) in float64 returns 3.330669 × 10⁻¹⁶, which is the printed m = 2 value to every digit printed, against a true tail of 3.8147 × 10⁻¹⁶; beyond roughly z = 9.4 the same subtraction underflows to exactly zero, which is what produces the two sentinels. The conclusion is accordingly stronger than any count of matching digits. Where 3D7 itself carries the resistance residue, the only annotation at that codon is the revertant, so a search for the resistance change matches nothing and the codon is reported as if it did not exist. This is exactly what happened at pfdhps 437 (Section 6.9.4). (ii) A residue reachable only by two changes within one codon is never annotated. pfcrt codon 75 spans Pf3D7_07_v3:403,621–403,623 and carries two variant records, 403621 (A>G, annotated `Asn75Asp`) and 403623 (T>A, annotated `Asn75Lys`). Asn→Glu requires both. Neither annotation names N75E, which is the residue the CVIET haplotype actually carries, so no string match could ever return it. The same mechanism accounts for pfk13 458, where the request was Asn458Tyr and the one variant isolate carries Asp (Section 6.8.3).

old: [Observed] Two points of context, both narrower than the previous version's. pfaat1 appears nowhere in the WHO compendium at any tier, so it is not "the most common validated resistance variant", which is what the previous version called it and which was a category error (Section 6.9.11). The replacement superlative has to be narrower still, and its exclusion rule stated: at 0.609, S258L is the most common variant in this panel with a published allele-replacement experiment behind it, outside the antifolates. It is not the most common resistance-associated non-antifolate variant, because pfmdr1 Y184F is higher at 0.677 (n = 1,858) and pfmdr2 I492V is close behind at 0.549; Y184F carries no WHO label either, so the tiers cannot be doing the excluding — what distinguishes S258L is comparable functional-replacement data, which Y184F does not have. It did not head that table, and the earlier phrasing that said it did is corrected here.

old: [Observed] Zone effects cannot be separated from sequencing-study effects either. This confounder was absent from the previous draft and is at least as serious as the collinearity above. Pf8 isolates arrive through named partner studies, and in Ghana those studies are almost perfectly nested within zones: four of six zone pairs share no sequencing study at all, including Coastal savanna vs Guinea savanna, the pair that produces the maximum FST and the polyclonality contrast. Three of the four zones are dominated by a single study — the transitional zone is one study outright (50 of 50 isolates, 1083-PF-GH-CONWAY), coastal savanna 89 per cent one study (387 of 435), Guinea savanna 74 per cent one study (2,678 of 3,605) — and deciduous forest is the only zone with no majority study, its largest contributing 391 of 815 (48 per cent). Batch effects in these data are demonstrable rather than hypothetical: holding zone constant so that only study varies, call rate differs between the six Guinea savanna studies at p = 2.8 × 10⁻¹⁹⁷, and between four of deciduous forest's five contributing studies at p = 7.7 × 10⁻⁸⁸ (the fifth, 1114-PF-PDN-DBS-GH-GHANSAH, contributes 4 isolates and was too small to enter the test). The Coastal–Guinea contrast has no within-study replicate and cannot be separated from a batch contrast by any reanalysis of these data. This applies with full force to the marker clines in §7.5: the pfaat1 S258L contrast runs between the two zones that share no study. See §9.1, limitation 2.

old: [Calculated] The outlier list is a ranking, and only part of it is a finding. Nineteen SNPs exceed the calibrated POD 0.999 quantile of 10.840; 3.9 false positives are expected at that threshold by construction, giving an empirical FDR of 20.6 per cent. Thirteen of the nineteen also survive Benjamini–Hochberg correction at q ≤ 0.10, and eight at q ≤ 0.01. Report the 13 as the finding and the 19 as a ranking. Seventeen of the nineteen fall in annotated genes — 13 genes in all, four of them carrying two SNPs each — and two are intergenic; one of those intergenic sites ranks fifth in the entire scan on XtX (20.79, q = 0.005), so the gene list is not simply the top of the ranking and should not be described as "19 outliers in 13 genes" — although that same site is now flagged lower confidence on variant-quality grounds (see the note below). Nothing about an elevated XtX value establishes that a locus is under selection rather than drifting unusually or sitting near an assembly or alignment artefact; a per-SNP variant-quality check has now closed the artefact reading for the set as a whole (next paragraph), but no quality check can convert a ranking into evidence of selection. The one partial exception is pfaat1 S258L: its XtX of 24.20 is the second-highest in the scan, behind PTP7 (Pf3D7_03_v3:96,476, XtX 26.44); it sits inside the FDR-10% set at q = 0.0049, which is now readable from the restored per-SNP table rather than only from the corrections record (see the note in §7.5); and it is the only outlier carrying a residue for which published gene-editing work exists. That functional support is real but modest and conditional, and the previous draft overstated it — see §7.5, where the experiment is described as its authors described it.

old: [Calculated] Likelihood monotonicity in TreeMix — now resolved. The log-likelihood never falls as migration edges are added — 89.65 at m = 0, 91.21 at m = 1, 92.23 at m = 2, 92.26 at m = 3, and 92.2642 at both m = 4 and m = 5, identical to the recorded precision — so likelihood cannot select a model, and the previous draft left the choice between m = 2 and m = 3 open. Re-running the sweep with -se settles it: the first two edges carry weights 0.152 (SE 0.048, p = 7.5 × 10⁻⁴) and 0.805 (SE 0.100, p = 3.3 × 10⁻¹⁶), while the third edge added at m = 3 has weight 0.065 (SE 0.147, p = 0.33) and is indistinguishable from zero. A two-edge graph is the model these data select, which also confirms from the statistics what was previously argued only from theory — that four populations can support only about two edges. The m = 2 vs m = 3 hedging in the previous draft is withdrawn.

(i) A results file was destroyed and restored. results/baypass/xtx_all_snps.csv was found at 0 bytes, truncated at 08:29:53 — hours after the 01:42 run that produced it, so almost certainly a stray shell redirect where a read was intended during a verification pass. It was the only zero-byte file under results/ or interim/. It was regenerated from the intact BayPass outputs, and the regeneration is provably faithful: outlier_snps.bed, xtx_calibration.json and xtx_threshold.txt are byte-identical by md5 before and after, and the restored file carries the same 3,916 rows and the same 19 outliers. The consequence is in fact positive — the per-SNP q-values are on disk again, so the pfaat1 q-value of 0.0049 and the tie between the two AAT1 SNPs are now reproducible from a primary output rather than from a narrative (§7.5 note). But the episode is also the clearest argument this project has produced for version control, which is gap (ii) in the paragraph below: nothing in the setup would have detected the truncation except someone opening the file. (ii) A log misreported its own output path. The --suffix patch to step03_umap.py suffixed the file writes but not the print statements, so the stage 3 re-run reported writing to the published dimred_comparison.csv when it had correctly written dimred_comparison_qcset.csv. No data were at risk — verified from the published file's mtime and contents — but a log that misstates where it wrote is exactly what causes a later misattribution, and this is one more instance of the pattern in §8.1: the defect was inside a correction, not inside the original code. Fixed.

old: [Interpreted] What the artemisinin negative is now worth, and what the kelch13 cross-check is worth. The result is a tested negative across the complete WHO-validated set rather than an untested absence, and that is the change that matters. Calling it the most policy-relevant result the analysis produces remains an assessment and not a finding, and three qualifications now attach to it. Surveillance for artemisinin resistance was not among the manuscript's stated objectives. The sampling period is 2009–2021. And the corroboration from MalariaGEN's own `kelch13` calls is much weaker than the previous version implied: Pf8 assigns a status over the whole 349–726 domain and classifies any missing call in that range as undetermined, so only 36 isolates have a complete published status — under 2 per cent of the sample — which is weak corroboration for per-codon calls on roughly 1,860 isolates. The two must not be presented as equivalent evidence. Among those 36, the commonest observed change is Ala578Ser, which is explicitly non-resistance.

[Calculated] Mixed-infection frequency does not order monotonically along the north–south gradient. In geographic order from north to south the polyclonal fraction is 0.597 in Guinea savanna (2,153 of 3,605), 0.500 in the transitional zone (25 of 50), 0.539 in deciduous forest (439 of 815) and 0.444 in coastal savanna (193 of 435). The transitional zone is the second-most-northern zone, lies north of the deciduous forest, breaks the trend, and at 25 of 50 carries no information. The original text quoted only the two endpoints. The gradient is also confounded with sequencing study, and the demonstration is in deciduous forest, not Guinea savanna: of the five studies contributing to deciduous forest, the four large enough to test (the fifth has 4 isolates) differ in Fws — Kruskal–Wallis H = 14.9, p = 1.9 x 10-3, n = 811 — and their polyclonal fractions span 0.430 to 0.578. The p-value belongs to the Fws distributions; no test of the polyclonal fraction itself exists in the outputs, and the 7.7 x 10-88 figure printed beside deciduous forest in the corrections document is its call-rate test, not its polyclonality. Guinea savanna is the wrong zone to cite here: its six studies span 0.532 to 0.682 but do not differ significantly (p = 0.103), so it is one of the two testable zones in which this batch effect cannot be demonstrated — coastal savanna is the other (two studies, n = 435, p = 0.378) — and the transitional zone, with a single study, cannot be tested at all. Of the three testable zones the effect is demonstrated in exactly one and cannot be demonstrated in two.

old: Reframe the thesis objectives in light of the collinearity, and in light of Objective 3 now being answered. The question "do ecological zones structure the parasite population?" cannot be answered with Pf8 metadata alone. Two questions that can be, and have been, are "is Ghanaian P. falciparum spatially structured at all, and what does that imply for surveillance design?" and "do resistance-marker frequencies vary across the country?" The second was originally written off as unanswerable from these data and is in fact the strongest result the analysis holds — with the caveat that it took two attempts to measure correctly. The first of those two questions now has a narrower answer than it did a revision ago: the structure is negligible and the distance gradient is not robust, so what the analysis establishes about space is a bound rather than a pattern, and the surveillance-design implication rests on the bound alone.

Analyse Fws by zone and year as a transmission-intensity phenotype in its own right, with study as a covariate, since the between-study variation within a single zone is of the same order as the between-zone variation: the polyclonal fraction (F<sub>ws</sub> < 0.95) spans 0.430 to 0.578 across the four testable studies in deciduous forest. Those two numbers are fractions of isolates below the monoclonality cut, not Fws values, and Section 10.1 labels them that way; the two statements must agree.
